newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices tread water as players watch EU.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices tread water as players watch EU.

text.p: Danish bond prices were static during Monday morning in thin trade, as players awaited signals from the EU summit. They was general optimism that leaders would agree an EMU budget stability pact.
"The market expects an agreement and has therefore risen a little, but it is very hesitant," a dealer said.

At 1145 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 traded at 112.30, yielding 6.13 percent, up from Friday's 112.11 but unchanged since early morning. The seven percent 2007 bond traded at 104.96, yielding 6.32 percent, 0.11 point up from Friday but also unchanged throughout the morning.

The crown firmed slightly, to 3.8064 to the mark from an earlier 3.8066. Turnover in the 2006 was a low 700 million crowns and the 2007 -- which becomes the benchmark on September 1 -- had volume of 250 million crowns.
The 2006 yield gap with Germany narrowed to 46 basis points from an earlier 48 bp and the 2007 gap to the bund closed one point to 65 bp.

The 2006's June future stood at 112.27, unchanged since the morning but up 0.13 from Friday.The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 slipped to 90.38 compared to an earlier 90.60 and Friday's 90.35. Copenhagen newsroom +45-33-969650
